abstract: We study the Nyman–Beurling spaces of $f_S=\zeta\prod_{q\in S}(1-q^{-s})$, the zeta function of the integers with no prime factor in a set $S$ of primes, with the random sifted control of Paper 116 as the main example: each prime is deleted with probability $p^{\alpha-1}$, $1/2<\alpha<1$, $f_S$ has a simple zero at $\alpha$, and under RH its integer error is $O(x^{\theta_*+\varepsilon})$ with $\theta_*<1/2$. First, unconditionally and by an elementary dilation argument, if $\sum_{q\in S}q^{-1/p}<\infty$ then the continuous and discrete $L^p(0,1)$ spans for $f_S$ coincide with those for $\zeta$. The reason is that $\prod_{q\in S}(1-q^{-s})$ is then a unit of the algebra of Dirichlet series with $\sum|a_n|n^{-1/p}<\infty$, which acts on $L^p(0,1)$ and preserves both spans. For the random control this gives, almost surely, closure in $L^p$ for $1<p<1/\alpha$ if and only if $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>1/p$. Second, Beurling's necessity functional gives non-closure for $1/\alpha<p<1/\theta_*$ under RH. Third, Burnol's exact distance formula holds for every Beurling system with integer error $O(x^\beta)$, $\beta<1/2$: the squared $L^2$ distance from $\mathbf 1_{(0,1]}$ to the span is $1-\prod|1-1/\rho|^2$ over zeros with $\operatorname{Re}\rho>1/2$, which is $(2\alpha-1)/\alpha^2$ for the control under RH. We compute discrete distances up to $N=200$ from exact Gram matrices and conjecture their limit $1/(\alpha^2K_S(\alpha,\alpha))$, which is $0.55615$ at $\alpha=0.6$. We show that $\sqrt{hk}\,G(h,k)$ depends only on $h/k$ for every $f$, and, under RH for $\alpha\le2/3$, that the exact exponential decay rate of the Gram kernel of $f_S$ is $(1-\alpha)/2$. Finally, asking for a statement about Nyman–Beurling data that is provable for $\zeta$ but false for the controls is degenerate. By Burnol and the verification of RH to height $3\cdot10^{12}$, "squared distance at most $10^{-11}$" is provable for $\zeta$ unconditionally and fails for the Davenport–Heilbronn function; under RH it fails for $f_S$ when $(2\alpha-1)/\alpha^2>10^{-11}$, though not for the whole family.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary: Corrections from the acceptance review; no change to the results. (1) Proof of Proposition 5.1: the uniqueness of the zero at alpha is stated for F_S on Re s > alpha/2 (Lemma 11 of Paper 116) and for f_S only on Re s > 1/2, which is what the argument uses since 1 - alpha/2 >= 2/3; the same precision is added where Theorem C is applied. (2) K_S(alpha,alpha) is now evaluated with a Hurwitz-zeta tail expansion (new script ks_hurwitz.py, replacing ks_em.py, whose quadrature tail was inaccurate): K_S(0.6,0.6) = 4.99463348 and the conjectured limit 0.556152, in agreement with the referee; the values at alpha = 0.55 in the supplement are corrected to 9.992824 and 0.330816. (3) The finite-U table entries are labelled d_{N,U}^2, and the text says the finite-U data do not establish Conjecture 4.1. (4) Section 6 and the abstract state the threshold as (2 alpha - 1)/alpha^2 > 10^{-11} (with the sufficient condition alpha >= 1/2 + 1.3e-12), and the Davenport-Heilbronn zero is sourced to the supplement of Paper 66. (5) Paper 22/v3, Theorem 6(a)-(b), is credited as the finite-S, p = 2 antecedent of Theorem A, and the extension is stated.
title: Nyman–Beurling spaces of sifted zeta functions
